hub.title: Books
hub.subtitle: Your accounts, worked out from every invoice, bill, payment and expense
hub.vouchersHint: Adjustments, cash to bank, GST and TDS entries
hub.costCentresHint: Projects and departments, for profit by each
hub.costCentreProfitHint: Income and expenses of each project or department
hub.profitLossHint: Trading account, then indirect income and expenses
hub.balanceSheetHint: What the business owns and owes
hub.closeHint: Lock a period once it is filed or audited
hub.integrityHint: The ledger against the invoices, payments, statements and stock it comes from

account.retainedEarnings: Profit and loss of earlier years
account.assetDisposal: Profit or loss on assets sold

accounts.name: Name
accounts.openingHint: The balance on the day your books begin, or on the date below.
accounts.openingOnDate: Opening balance as on a date
accounts.openingOnDateHint: Off: it stands at the start of your books.

vouchers.emptyBody: Record adjustments, cash put in the bank, GST set-offs and TDS paid to the government.

kindHint.journal: Any adjustment: depreciation, provisions, a refund, a correction.
kindHint.contra: Money between cash and bank: a deposit, a withdrawal, a transfer.
kindHint.gstJournal: Adjustments to the GST ledgers: a credit reversed, interest, a set-off.
kindHint.tdsChallan: TDS paid to the government, from the challan.
kindHint.receipt: Money in that isn't from an invoice, into cash or bank.
kindHint.gstChallan: GST paid into the portal’s cash ledger (PMT-06), head by head.

vouchers.referenceHint: A challan number and BSR code, or a cheque number.
vouchers.deleteMessage: Its entries come off the books.
vouchers.reservesNeedNarration: Say why earlier years’ profit changes: add a narration
vouchers.unbalanced: Debits and credits must be equal
vouchers.needsTwo: A voucher needs at least two lines
vouchers.bsrHint: The bank branch's 7-digit code, on the challan
vouchers.challanInvalid: A BSR code has 7 digits and a challan serial up to 5
vouchers.draftHint: Not in the books yet. It takes a number and reaches the ledgers when you post it.

tb.basis: Balances for the period; income and expenses start the financial year at zero
tb.unbalanced: Out by {{amount}}: report this to support

pl.basis: The period's income and expenses, with stock valued from the stock ledger

bs.basis: On the last day of the period
bs.currentProfit: Profit for the year so far
bs.currentLoss: Loss for the year so far
bs.differs: The two sides differ by {{amount}}: report this to support

dayBook.basis: Every entry in the period, with its debits and credits

costCentres.name: Name
costCentres.emptyBody: Add a project or department, then tag invoices, bills, expenses and journal lines with it to see what each earns and costs.
costCentres.basis: From the books. Stock isn’t split by cost centre, so the rows add up to the profit before the change in stock.
costCentres.nothing: Nothing tagged with a cost centre in this period.

close.body: Nothing dated on or before the close can be added, changed or removed: invoices, bills, notes, payments, expenses and vouchers. Filing GSTR-3B closes its month on its own.
close.throughHint: Usually the last day of a filed month, or of the audited year
close.reopenHint: Reopening lets the closed period change again. Anything changed there may no longer match what was filed or audited.
close.closeAskBody: Nothing dated on or before {{date}} can be added, changed or removed until an owner reopens the books.
close.reopenAskBody: Everything through {{date}} can be changed again. Anything changed there may no longer match what was filed or audited.
close.ownerOnly: Only an owner can close or reopen the books.
close.periodic: Periodic: closing stock is valued from the stock ledger at the end of each period, as in Tally.
close.perpetualSince: Perpetual since {{date}}: goods are posted to Stock in hand at cost as they come in and go out, and what is sold to Cost of goods sold.
close.perpetualBody: Perpetual stock starts on the first day of a financial year that is still open. Earlier years stay periodic, with the stock they closed with.
close.turnOnBody: From {{date}}, goods are posted to Stock in hand as they come in and go out, and the profit and loss shows Cost of goods sold instead of opening and closing stock. Reports from that day change. You can go back to periodic while that year is open.
close.turnOffBody: Stock from {{date}} is valued at the end of each period again, and nothing is posted to Stock in hand or Cost of goods sold. Reports from that day change.

costingBody.average: Goods going out are costed at the average of what is in stock, which moves with each purchase.
costingBody.fifo: Goods going out are costed at what the oldest stock still on hand cost; stock left over is valued at the latest prices.

close.costingLocked: Stock costing values every period's stock, so it can be changed only while no period is closed.
close.costingAskBody: Every period's stock value and cost of goods sold is worked out again this way, from when the books began. Reports change. Keep the method you choose year after year (AS 2).

costingSaved.average: Stock is costed at weighted average
costingSaved.fifo: Stock is costed first in, first out

receipts.title: Receipts
receipts.emptyBody: Money in that isn't from an invoice: interest, rent, a refund, capital brought in.
receipts.sourceHint: Interest, rent, a refund. Taxable income goes on an invoice.
receipts.attachHint: A photo of the cheque, deposit slip or letter
receipts.emptyFiltered: Nothing matches. Try another period or search.

integrity.basis: Checked as of the last day of the period

key.stock: Stock ledger matches stock in hand
key.allocations: No document paid more than its total

hint.sourcesBalance: Debits equal credits for each invoice, bill, payment, expense and voucher
hint.roundOff: No document rounds off by a rupee or more
hint.partyLedgers: Each party billed in rupees: its statement against its account in the books
hint.stock: Under perpetual stock: the stock account against the stock ledger’s value
hint.allocations: Money set against each invoice or bill is no more than it is for

openings.title: Import what was outstanding
openings.hint: Invoices or bills still unpaid when you started using these books, one row each: party (name or GSTIN), number, date, due date and the amount still outstanding. They go on each party’s account and in aging, against Opening balances; never in sales, purchases or GST. A party with an opening balance already is left out, so nothing is counted twice.

forecast.title: Cash-flow forecast
forecast.basis: Cash and bank today, plus what customers owe by due date, less bills by due date, plus recurring invoices and expenses. Overdue amounts count in the first week.
forecast.shortfall: Runs short in the week from {{date}}

journalImport.title: Import journals
journalImport.hint: One row per line: date, reference, account, debit, credit and narration. Rows with the same reference make one journal. Accounts are matched by name.
journalImport.asDraftsHint: Drafts can be unbalanced and don't reach the books until posted.
journalImport.missingColumns: The sheet needs Date and Account columns.
journalImport.tooMany: Up to 500 journals at a time.

assets.title: Fixed assets
assets.notFound: This asset isn't in the register
assets.intro: What the business owns and uses for more than a year: machinery, computers, vehicles, furniture. Its cost is in the books from the bill it was bought on; the register writes it off month by month.
assets.emptyBody: Add each machine, computer or vehicle bought on a bill, and its depreciation posts to the books at each month's end.
assets.scheduleHint: Cost and depreciation for the year, as the notes to the accounts show them
assets.scheduleBasis: Cost and depreciation at the start, what was bought, written off and disposed of, and at the end.
assets.name: Asset
assets.accountHint: The fixed-asset account its bill or voucher put the cost in
assets.costHint: What it cost, before GST you claim back
assets.residualHint: What it should fetch at the end; never written off
assets.slmHint: Cost less residual value, evenly over its life, by the day (Schedule II)
assets.wdvHint: The rate on what is left at the start of each year, by the days it was in use
assets.brought: Bought before the books began here
assets.broughtHint: Give the depreciation already written off, and the day it stood at
assets.disposedHint: Sold, scrapped or lost: depreciation stops that day, and it leaves the books. Record what it fetched as a receipt to Profit or loss on assets sold.
assets.inUseBeforeAcquired: It is put to use on or after the day it was acquired
assets.removeBody: Its depreciation comes out of the books. Its cost of {{cost}} stays where its bill or voucher put it.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.intro: Plan what each income and expense account should come to over a year, then see how the books are doing against it.
budgets.emptyBody: Set a figure for sales and each expense for the year, and see each month how the books compare.
budgets.name: Name
budgets.annualHint: Spread evenly over the months; open the months to set any on its own
budgets.removeBody: Only the plan goes; the books stay as they are.
budgets.basis: What was planned for the period against what the books show. A month the period covers only in part is planned in proportion to its days.

adjust.title: Adjust advance
adjust.intro: Apply what a party has paid in advance, or a credit note not raised against an invoice, to what they still owe.
adjust.noCredit: No unadjusted advance or credit note
adjust.noOpen: Nothing is owed on an invoice or note
adjust.emptyHint: Advances and direct credit notes show here once there is something open to apply them to.
adjust.notService: This invoice has no service on it: GST paid on a service advance should only come back on a service invoice.
adjust.autoNotService: Some open invoices have no service on them; a service advance applied to one takes its GST back on goods. Choose by hand to avoid that.
adjust.over: More than is left of it ({{amount}})
adjust.applyAllHint: Or pick an advance above to choose where it goes.

transfer.title: Transfer
transfer.hint: Move money between your cash and bank accounts: a deposit, a withdrawal or a bank-to-bank transfer. It is posted as a contra voucher.
transfer.pickAccount: Pick a cash or bank account
transfer.referenceHint: A cheque, UTR or slip number.
